_note: Run MECHANICS -- how a batch executes, independent of which league or decks. Pass alongside a league-identity config (--run-config this, --league-config that), or let a league config inherit these directly via its own top-level "extends": "run_default.json" (see league_main.json, run_gauntlet_twin.json, run_bench.json -- all three do this now instead of retyping the fields below, so they can never drift from this file). checkpoint_opponent_rate is the one field meant to be overridden per-invocation rather than edited here. Fields that are absent are absent on purpose: games_per_iteration below overrides it, but with no override run_league derives max(1, n_workers) (one game per worker, per its own benchmark comment); the PPO batch-size ramp is hardcoded in rl.train.batch_size_for_iteration; and max_batch_size's safety role belongs to whatever repeatedly re-invokes run_league.py and health-checks between batches.
_values_note: The two non-obvious values, both set 2026-08-13 and both still current. games_per_iteration 24 (not n_workers=6): at 6, every ppo_update spent its whole trust region on six games and approx_kl measured 0.044 against target_kl 0.03 -- early stopping on most updates, epochs_run falling 3.8 -> 2.8 over a run. The larger buffer costs wall-clock without adding collection parallelism; that is the deliberate trade. pfsp_power 0.5 (not 2.0): 2.0 was backwards and sent three of four decks into 58-77% of their games in matchups they win under 25% of -- see rl/league.py's own comment for the measurement.
_identity_note: The 4-deck sub-league is the experiment vehicle for the 2026-08 plateau investigation. Regrown from scratch after the 2026-08-17 per-deck-encoder change and trained to 10,008 games/deck on 2026-08-18; the twin at gauntlet_league_name was then grown to 5,016 games/deck against it, so vs_gauntlet is live in BOTH directions now rather than the no-op it was while the twin did not exist. Note this league's own metrics.jsonl carries no vs_gauntlet records for that first 10,008 games: the twin had no live.pt yet, which is the documented None case, not a failure.
